item.title: Spherical orbits around a Newman-Janis-generated rotating Bronnikov black hole
item.description: arXiv:2611.28074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate spherical geodesics in a Newman--Janis-generated rotating regular geometry constructed from the magnetically-charged Bronnikov mass profile. The Kretschmann scalar is exponentially suppressed at the center, and is smooth across the disk and ring within the single-sheeted domain $r\geq0$. We show that all physically admissible spherical photon orbits outside the event horizon are radially unstable in the black-hole regime, whereas stable spherical photon orbits can exist in horizonless configurations. The unstable photon orbits determine the shadow, which for an edge-on observer is smaller and distorted compared with the Kerr shadow. For timelike motion, we identify marginally stable spherical orbits and determine the innermost stable spherical orbit (ISSO). We further examine the null, weak, strong, and dominant energy conditions, finding violations in the strong-field region but satisfaction of all four conditions asymptotically and throughout the exterior of every black-hole configuration. Together with stable causality and the curvature bound, these results show that the metric satisfies the five geometric criteria C1--C5 proposed by Maeda for physically reasonable nonsingular black holes.
item.dc:creator: F. Subandi, H. S. Ramadhan

item.title: Curvature-history tensor memory in inflationary cosmology: Component closure, ghost-free dynamics, and CMB BipoSH likelihood
item.description:
arXiv:2611.28106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a generally covariant inflationary model in which curvature history activates a spatial symmetric-tracefree tensor-memory order parameter and generates a scale-dependent quadrupolar departure from primordial statistical isotropy. The curvature source is the four-dimensional Gauss--Bonnet completion of the Kretschmann invariant. A local $(C,\chi)$ representation is used only to implement the retarded theory: fixed retarded Cauchy data remove the homogeneous response modes, so the negative-sign localized combination is not an independent phase-space degree of freedom. The projected tensor sector is described by the dressed field $Q_{\mu
u}=\mathcal E_C\widehat Q_{\mu
u}$ with $\mathcal E_C=\exp[B(C)\Box_{\widehat Q}/2]$. Its raw-field Hessian has the exact congruence form $\mathcal E_C^\dagger(\Box_Q-\mathsf M^2)\mathcal E_C$, so an invertible dressing preserves the solution count and the sign of the physical symplectic norm even when $[B(C),\Box_Q]
e0$. We derive the full quadratic Hessian, eliminate the ADM constraints and retarded response variables through an exact block Schur complement, and obtain the leading anisotropic curvature action. A nonlinear ADM Legendre analysis shows that the representative inflationary solution remains far from the singular threshold associated with an Ostrogradsky branch. A smooth curvature-dependent phase potential gives an approximately constant activated plateau with subdominant memory energy. Finite activation then produces an infrared-regular oscillatory primordial quadrupole and an exact scale-dependent $T/E$ BipoSH covariance. We also give the corresponding cut-sky Gaussian and quadratic maximum-likelihood estimators.
item.dc:creator: G. M. Rhythm

item.title: Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity corrections in Dark Dimension scenario
item.description: arXiv:2611.28132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the thermodynamics, dynamical stability, and phenomenological implications of Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet (EGB) black holes in Dark Dimension scenarios with one or two micron-sized extra dimensions. For the asymptotically flat, neutral Boulware-Deser solution with positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling $\alpha$, we derive the mass, Hawking temperature, Wald entropy, and heat capacity in arbitrary dimension $D\ge 5$. A positive-heat-capacity branch arises only in $D=5$, where the temperature peaks at $T_{\max}=1/(8\pi\sqrt{\alpha})$ at $r_h=2\sqrt{\alpha}$ and vanishes in the zero-radius limit at finite mass $M_{\rm lim}=3\pi\alpha/(4G_5)$. For $G_5=(8\pi M_*^3)^{-1}$, $\alpha=M_*^{-2}$, and $M_*\sim 10^{10}$ GeV, this yields $M_{\rm lim}\simeq 1.06\times 10^{-12}$ g. While this branch formally overlaps with classical instability zones, the string ultraviolet cutoff safely suppresses the responsible high-harmonic modes. Assuming a UV completion stabilizes these relics, we show they can constitute all of cold dark matter. We map their observational signatures, highlighting a scalar-induced gravitational-wave peak at 33 THz and the suppression of Hawking bursts. In $D=6$, the heat capacity is negative at all radii. Within a bulk blackbody emission model, we derive the leading large-mass lifetime correction and the small-radius scaling $\tau\propto M_0^3$, compared to $\tau_{\rm GR}\propto M_0^{5/3}$. For $M_*\sim 10$ TeV, we identify distinct collider benchmarks: a steeper energy scaling for the production cross section and a suppressed decay multiplicity ($\langle N \rangle \sim 4$). These provide clear experimental signatures distinguishing 6D EGB gravity from classical General Relativity, mapping the transition toward the string scale.
item.dc:creator: George K. Leontaris, George Prampromis

item.title: Generalization of the Theory of Relativity Based on Finsler Geometry, Incorporating a Fundamental Mass at High Energies
item.description: arXiv:2611.28141v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We generalize special and general relativity so that, besides the speed of light $c$, an invariant fundamental mass $M$ bounds the energy of every massive particle. The exact Legendre transform of a projectively deformed mass shell gives, for a particle of mass $m$, a closed-form Finsler function $F_\mu$, $\mu=m/M$: a Lorentzian Randers metric built from the spacetime metric $g$ and a unit timelike covector $u$. Its indicatrix is the Minkowski hyperboloid displaced by $W=\mu u/(1+\mu)$, so $F_\mu$ is a Zermelo navigation metric whose symmetry group, the Lorentz group centred at $W$, realizes a relativity principle with two invariants, $c$ and $M$. Light propagates exactly as in Einstein's theory, while massive particles obey $E<M$, a deformed time-dilation law and a composition-dependent free fall, $\eta\simeq\Delta m/M$. The Finsler--Einstein tensor equation, solved exactly for a spatially flat universe, gives Friedmann equations with corrections $\propto\mu\dot H$ and leaves de~Sitter space exact. Observed particle energies, equivalence-principle tests and electron-EDM limits constrain $M$. The construction makes Kadyshevsky's fundamental-mass hypothesis geometric and testable.
item.dc:creator: Rustam Ibadov

item.title: Imprints of perfect fluid dark matter distributions and topological defects on Born--Infeld AdS black hole signatures
item.description: arXiv:2611.28143v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a static, spherically symmetric \BI{} \AdS{} \BH{} that carries a topological defect, either a \GM{} or a \CS{}, and is immersed in \PFDM{}. The metric function collects four independent deformations of the Schwarzschild geometry: a constant solid-angle deficit $(1-\xi)$ from the defect, the nonlinear charge sector controlled by the \BI{} scale $\beta$, the logarithmic \PFDM{} term set by the intensity $\lambda$, and the \AdS{} curvature $\Lambda$. We verify that the solution reduces to the charged \AdS{}--\PFDM{} defect geometry as $\beta \to \infty$ and to Schwarzschild when all deformations switch off. The horizon, photon sphere, and shadow all grow monotonically with the defect strength $\xi$. We compute the innermost stable circular orbit and the epicyclic frequencies, read off the relativistic-precession predictions for twin-peak quasi-periodic oscillations, and confront them with five accreting sources through a Markov chain Monte Carlo fit. For spin-0 perturbations we obtain the scalar potential, the higher-order WKB \QNM{} spectrum, and the \GBF{}, all of which soften as $\xi$ rises. The extended phase space analysis yields a \VdW{}-type $P$--$V$ structure whose critical point shifts with the defect, the \BI{} scale, and the halo intensity. Throughout, the four sectors leave distinct imprints on imaging, timing, ringdown, and thermal channels, {\color{black} which we read as parameter sensitivities rather than as an observational separation of the four, a distinction a joint multichannel fit would be needed to settle}.
item.dc:creator: Faizuddin Ahmed, Ahmad Al-Badawi, \.{I}zzet Sakall{\i}

item.title: Stationary branches of non-canonical spinor theories and their cosmology
item.description: arXiv:2611.28149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a classical spinor field minimally coupled to gravity and described by a non-canonical Lagrangian depending on the fermionic kinetic scalar and the scalar bilinear. For purely kinetic theories, we show that the field equations split the solutions into two distinct branches. On the regular branch, the spinor satisfies the massless Dirac equation and contributes a vacuum energy determined by an additive constant in the Lagrangian. On the stationary branch, the spinor field equations become identically satisfied, while the energy-momentum tensor is exactly that of a cosmological constant for any spinor configuration and in any spacetime. The spinor evolution is therefore not uniquely determined by the field equations. In a spatially flat homogeneous universe, both branches act as cosmological-constant sources. We also give the dilution law for homogeneous configurations in theories with explicit dependence on the scalar bilinear. When a potential with a nonzero minimum is introduced, the stationary configuration becomes the late-time state of the cosmological evolution, and the approach to it generates a pressureless component in addition to an effective cosmological constant. For a simple quadratic model, the background expansion reproduces exactly that of the standard $\Lambda$CDM cosmology, while the value of the vacuum energy remains controlled by an additive constant in the Lagrangian.
item.dc:creator: Ugo Moschella, Mario Novello, Oliver F. Piattella

item.title: Primordial black holes production in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.28150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider models with the Gauss-Bonnet term multiplied to a function of the scalar field and propose a new inflationary model which provides a mechanism for the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs). For certain values of the model parameters, the predictions of this model agree with observational data from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). Due to estimation of possiable PBHs masses, we demonstrate that they can be considered as a possible source for all or part of dark matter.
item.dc:creator: Ekaterina O. Pozdeeva, Sergey Yu. Vernov

item.title: Optical appearance of a non-commutative black hole surrounded by an accretion disk
item.description: arXiv:2611.28151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the optical appearance of a non--commutative Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a transparent, geometrically thin emitting disk. A Lorentzian matter distribution supplies the effective exterior metric. We compute photon trajectories, disk transfer functions, and the observed bolometric intensity for static and circular emitters, taking into account gravitational redshift, orbital time dilation, and Doppler modulation. At fixed asymptotic mass, increasing $\theta=\Theta/M^2$ from zero to $0.03$ reduces the critical impact parameter by approximately $16.1\%$ and the innermost stable circular orbit radius by $23.7\%$. The narrow higher-order features follow this contraction, while the broad direct peak shifts by less than $1\%$ for a fixed emission profile. With the same source normalization, the peak direct intensity and the signal integrated over the screen aperture increase by approximately $6.5\%$ and $4.3\%$, respectively. Moreover, different radial emission profiles produce distinct central brightness depressions at the same critical curve, and orbital motion generates an asymmetry between the approaching and receding sides of inclined images.
item.dc:creator: Adailton Azev\^edo Ara\'ujo Filho, Narges Heidari, Alesandro Ferreira dos Santos, Shahin Mamedov, Valdir Barbosa Bezerra, Amilcar Rabelo de Queiroz, Ali \"Ovg\"un

item.title: Spin-Torsion Coupling: Vector and Scalar Torsional Potentials of Chiral Spinor Currents
item.description: arXiv:2611.28182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate integral representations of torsional fields sourced by chiral spinor currents within a weak-field, Ricci-flow-inspired geometric framework. Starting from the coupling between spinorial currents and axial torsion, we construct screened Green-kernel solutions and examine their relation to antisymmetric tetradic perturbations and contorsion. Particular attention is devoted to stationary toroidal configurations, for which the magnetic-type dipole moment vanishes while a nonzero toroidal moment and effective circulation remain. The dependence of these quantities on Yukawa screening is analyzed, together with their implications for an Aharonov-Bohm-like geometric structure. We further introduce a mixed-chirality source describing an effective connection between oppositely polarized domains and investigate the corresponding flip-sector integral. The dynamics of massive Majorana neutrinos in an axial background is then examined, distinguishing chiral mixing from helicity oscillations and identifying the role of transverse torsional components. The resulting framework connects spinorial sources, finite-range torsional potentials, toroidal geometry, and neutrino spin dynamics, while providing a mathematical basis for further investigations of torsional transport and observable effects.
item.dc:creator: Elisa Varani

item.title: Kinetic moment estimates and a one-sided Lyapunov barrier for the relativistic fermionic Michie-King equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.28278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the cutoff Ruffini--Arg\"uelles--Rueda (RAR), or relativistic fermionic Michie--King, equation of state along an equilibrium family with fixed Tolman--Klein invariants. Three kinetic moments give exact formulas for both the pressure-to-density ratio and the derivative of pressure. Cauchy--Schwarz yields a global relation between these two quantities. It implies vertical vector-field domination of the associated Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff system by the linear equation of state $P=\rho c^2/\sqrt3$ in the physical wedge $0<y\leq3x$. We construct a filled, one-sided version of the Bors--Sta\'nczy Lyapunov barrier and check every boundary. This controls all outward excursions, including those after a lower exit from a Lyapunov sublevel. For regular configurations the resulting explicit Lambert bound is $2Gm(r)/(rc^2)<0.6879212521$. Using the diagonal where this ratio has a stationary value sharpens the bound to $0.6734385929$. The argument is conditional on a regular TOV configuration and does not require a separate finite-radius existence theorem. We also identify and correct a logarithmic coefficient in the previously used explicit linear-comparator formula.
item.dc:creator: Dorota Bors, Robert Sta\'nczy

item.title: Radial stability of nonlinearly scalarized black holes in Einstein-phantom scalar-Gauss-Bonnet theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.28523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the radial stability of nonlinearly scalarized black holes found in Einstein--phantom scalar--Gauss--Bonnet theory with polynomial and exponential couplings. Two branches of lower and primary are found for phantom scalarized black holes. The coupled scalar--metric perturbations reduce to a Schr\"odinger-type equation, after eliminating redundant metric perturbations. The lower branch including the pure quartic solutions has one growing mode, while positive zero-energy solutions for the primary branch could establish stability through the $S$-deformation method. Stable primary solutions are found for the exponential coupling. Also, we explore the connection between radial stability and thermodynamic analysis for two branches. Furthermore, we show that canonical scalarized black holes obtained from Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet theory with polynomial coupling reveals unstable lower and stable primary branches.
item.dc:creator: De-Cheng Zou, Yun Soo Myung, Meng-Yun Lai, Hyat Huang, Wen-Cong Gan

item.title: Numerical Integration of Geodesic Motion in Non-Schwarzschild Spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2611.28694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This contribution presents a method for numerically solving geodesic motion in Wolfram Mathematica applied on a system consisting of a Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a thin Vogt-Letelier disk. While geodesic motion in the Schwarzschild spacetime is fully integrable due to its high degree of symmetry, the addition of a disk breaks the spherical symmetry and leads to a weak-integrable dynamical system. Particular attention is paid to the treatment of particle trajectories near the thin disk, where discontinuities in the derivatives of the metric may affect numerical stability and the conservation of integrals of motion. Several numerical treatments of disk crossings were implemented, arriving to a method based on the re-normalization of the four-velocity. The phase-space of the system is investigated using Poincar\'{e} sections and rotation number spectra.
item.dc:creator: Jan Pij\'{a}\v{c}ek, Georgios Lukes-Gerakopoulos, Ond\v{r}ej Zelenka

item.title: Exactly solvable Brill waves: explicit gravitational-wave initial data with trapped surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.28758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vacuum initial data for pure gravitational waves on $\mathbb{R}^3$ (Brill waves) have so far been obtained only numerically. Here a one-parameter family is solved exactly: in toroidal coordinates the constraint separates, and a suitable seed function makes every mode equation hypergeometric. The data are real analytic and asymptotically flat and exist precisely for $k<k_c=0.8048\ldots$; their mass is an explicit series with a pole at $k_c$. Near $k_c$ the data provably contain trapped surfaces and an apparent horizon. A scaling symmetry yields further solvable families, one of them elementary.
item.dc:creator: Piotr Koc

item.title: Anti-de Sitter charges and maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.28989v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct conserved charges of asymptotic symmetries for negative-cosmological-constant vacuum spacetimes from the Neumann data for the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints on maximal conformally-compact Cauchy hypersurfaces. This gives a general and canonical initial value treatment of charges for vacuum spacetimes with timelike conformal boundary.
item.dc:creator: A. Rod Gover, Jaros\l aw Kopi\'nski, Andrew Waldron

item.title: The shadow of rotating FJNW metric
item.description: arXiv:2611.28990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the astrophysical aspects of the rotating Fisher-Janis-Newman-Winicour (FJNW) metric recently derived in [1]. The Hamilton-Jacobi equation is used to obtain the shadow of the rotating FJNW metric. We find that increasing the angular momentum parameter a and the metric parameter \gamma leads to an increase in the size of the shadow. Finally, we study the deflection angle of light in the rotating FJNW spacetime.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: International Journal of Geometric Methods in Modern Physics (2026) 2750017
item.dc:creator: Mina Shokrollahi, Behrouz Mirza, Mahnaz Tavakoli Kachi

item.title: Unruh-like effects and correlation harvesting between particle detectors in uniform motion in (2+1)-dimensional Minkowski spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2611.29038v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Gaussian-switched Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the (2+1)-dimensional Minkowski vacuum and following four classes of uniformly accelerated trajectories: linear, catenary, cusped, and circular motion. We first determine how the single-detector transition probability and effective temperature depend on acceleration and the torsion-to-acceleration ratio $\bar{b}$, whose continuous variation connects these four trajectory classes. We find that both quantities generally increase with acceleration, while their dependence on $\bar{b}$ can become nonmonotonic depending on the energy gap. We also examine a correlation-harvesting protocol by two detectors following horizontally displaced copies of the same trajectory. Increasing acceleration or separation generally suppresses the harvested concurrence and quantum mutual information, but the extent of suppression at fixed acceleration depends strongly on the trajectory class. For each of the four trajectory classes, we identify regimes of genuine entanglement harvesting in which vacuum correlations alone suffice to entangle the detectors, while the communication contribution alone cannot overcome local noise.
item.dc:creator: Siwei Han, Zeinab Imani, Jun Feng, Robert B. Mann

item.title: Quasinormal Modes and Excitation Factors of a Parity-Symmetric Beyond-Horndeski Black Hole
item.description: arXiv:2611.29052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study scalar, electromagnetic, and Dirac perturbations of an asymptotically flat black hole in parity-symmetric beyond-Horndeski gravity. The quasinormal spectrum is computed with very-high-order WKB expansions and Pad\'e resummation, with Ces\`aro means used to diagnose internal convergence. The dominant modes are independently tested by time-domain evolution with Prony extraction and by Chebyshev pseudospectral collocation; the latter also provides systematic frequency scans in both the metric-scale and physical ADM-mass normalizations. Excitation factors are obtained separately from Green-function residues by complex-contour integration. In the fixed metric-scale normalization, approaching Schwarzschild generally increases both the oscillation frequency and damping rate, whereas stronger deformation shifts the modes toward lower frequencies and weaker damping. In ADM-mass units, the mildly deformed solutions remain close to Schwarzschild, while the most deformed sector becomes enhanced and nonmonotonic because the asymptotic mass itself varies strongly. The independent methods agree very well, however the sixth-order WKB approximation used in [G. Antoniou, T. D. Pappas, P. Kanti, Phys. Rev. D 112, 084013 (2025)] is insufficient in certain regions of the parameter space: the fundamental-mode discrepancy reaches nine percent in the damping rate and the first-overtone discrepancy can be of order unity. The Schwarzschild excitation factors are recovered. In the strongly deformed regime, their magnitudes can differ from the Schwarzschild values by more than two orders of magnitude in the asymptotic tortoise-coordinate convention. We show that this large effect is predominantly due to the deformation-dependent displacement of the potential barrier in the tortoise coordinate: when its maximum is used as the origin, the excitation factors exhibit much more modest deviations.
item.dc:creator: Roman A. Konoplya, Milena Skvortsova

item.title: The Schwarzschild Ringdown Time Prescription on Critical Kerr Plunges
item.description: arXiv:2611.29054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a Schwarzschild plunge, constant-amplitude quasinormal-mode convergence has been tied to the source's advanced time at $r=0$, lying $9.435M$ after the $(2,2)$ strain peak. On real prograde critical Kerr plunges, $P(r_-)<0$ forces the ingoing time $v$ to diverge logarithmically at the inner horizon while $u_K$ stays finite. Matching $v$ to $-u_K$ at the unique interior zero $P(r_0)=0$ yields a parameter-free onset hierarchy $(u_{\rm H},u_{r_0},u_{\rm C})$ that recovers $9.435M$ as $a\to 0$ and predicts two-stage residual decay and frequency locking at $(6.85M,11.35M,13.35M)$ on an $a/M=0.9$ eccentric plunge.
item.dc:creator: Jingxu Wu, Junyi Zhang, Daniil Stepanenko, Maxim Khlopov

item.title: QTG minimons
item.description: arXiv:2611.29109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study static, spherically symmetric, regular horizonless solutions of quasitopological gravity (QTG), which we call QTG minimons. These configurations form the small-mass branch below the threshold for regular black holes. We include vacuum polarization by coupling the spherically reduced QTG action to the Polyakov action for two-dimensional conformal matter. For an arbitrary characteristic function $h(p)$, we derive a constrained first-order system in the static, asymptotically empty state. We obtain central expansions in $D\ge4$ and analyze four-dimensional solutions in the Hayward-type and Born--Infeld-type models. Both models retain a de Sitter-like core. Along the near-critical branch, the asymptotic mass decreases with the quantum coupling, while the central blueshift can become large even for a small coupling. The numerical results indicate that vacuum polarization is a nonuniform perturbation near the critical limit. Assuming a smooth constant-radius limit in proper distance, we derive a candidate $\mathrm{AdS}_2\times S^{D-2}$ throat geometry for the limiting configurations, which we call QTG extremons.
item.dc:creator: Valeri P. Frolov

item.title: Quantum coherence and entanglement of mixed states in relativistic settings
item.description: arXiv:2611.29322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: States prepared in laboratory experiments are generally mixed because of imperfect preparation and residual coupling to the environment, whereas pure initial states represent an idealized limit. Motivated by this distinction, we investigate quantum entanglement and coherence in a pair of Unruh-DeWitt detectors initially prepared in a general two-qubit X state. One detector remains inertial and uncoupled, while the other undergoes uniform acceleration and interacts locally with a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum. We obtain the reduced detector state within a perturbative treatment and evaluate its concurrence, $l_1$ norm of coherence, and relative entropy of coherence. For the initial-state families considered, the resulting expressions exhibit entanglement sudden death at finite acceleration, with larger initial entanglement associated with a higher threshold. Both coherence measures remain nonzero beyond this threshold and approach zero in the formal infinite-acceleration limit of these expressions. We also examine the dependence of these resources on the detector energy gap and interaction duration. The results distinguish the persistence of coherence from that of entanglement in the mixed-state detector model and identify initial mixedness as a relevant ingredient in relativistic quantum information.
item.dc:creator: Xing-Le Zhao, Zhen Yang, Shu-Min Wu

item.title: Regge calculus for $f(R)$ gravity with torsion
item.description: arXiv:2611.29447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate $f(R)$ gravity with spacetime torsion in Regge calculus, but without an \emph{ad hoc} geometric definition of torsion. Working in D'Adda's formulation of simplicial gravity with coordinates, we show that the axial sector of the torsion is carried by a massless Kalb--Ramond two-form, which in four dimensions is dual to a single scalar on the dual vertices. The discretized theory is therefore pure Regge gravity coupled to two scalar fields, the scalaron and the axion, without a geometric definition of torsion on the Regge lattice. We derive the lattice action and the complete set of discrete equations of motion, and we verify the continuum limit. For a homogeneous and isotropic lattice we obtain the discrete Friedmann--Raychaudhuri system, compute the exact kinetic and curvature coefficients for a regular triangulation of $\mathbb S^3$, and show that the discrete equations reproduce the continuum closed solution at first order in the evolution time step. The results therefore present a very special case in which the torsional effects are completely described by scalar fields on the Regge lattice and there is no need of a full discrete differential calculus.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Kan Guo

item.title: Birefringent Imaging and Interferometry with Periodic Orbits and Accretion in Einstein-nonlinear-electrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.29472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate birefringent imaging, interferometric visibility, neutral periodic geodesics, and thin-disk radiation around a magnetically charged black hole in Einstein-nonlinearelectrodynamics, using the Euler-Heisenberg-type model of de Paula et al. [14]. The nonlinear coupling is treated as a free model parameter. Two effective photon metrics give rise to distinct unstable light rings, capture thresholds, and images. Transforming their image-order intensities into signed Fourier visibilities reveals separate critical-curve oscillations and a narrow-ring modulation scale in the unresolved sum. This two-mode correspondence does not require photon motion between two potential barriers. Rational orbital frequencies are then used to classify neutral bound trajectories and provide conservative gravitationalwave snapshots relevant to extreme-mass-ratio inspirals. A stationary thin-disk calculation supplies flux, temperature, emitted efficiency, and polarization-resolved thermal spectra. Across the sampled parameters, magnetic charge dominates the changes, while matched Maxwell comparisons resolve smaller nonlinear corrections. The static, optically thin emitters and the orbiting, optically thick thermal disk are distinct source configurations. Polarization comparisons use the same material source within each configuration; their brightness and spectral results are conditional on that configuration.
item.dc:creator: Shi-Hai Dong, Farokhnaz Hosseinifar, Orlando Luongo, Hassan Hassanabadi

item.title: Viscous damping of axisymmetric oscillation modes of uniformly rotating relativistic stars
item.description: arXiv:2611.29617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the effects of bulk and shear viscosity on the damping of axisymmetric oscillations of uniformly rotating relativistic stars, using the first-order viscous hydrodynamics formulation of Bemfica, Disconzi, Noronha and Kovtun (BDNK). The equations of motion are implemented in a two-dimensional numerical code under the Cowling approximation, assuming the fluid evolves on the fixed spacetime of a rotating star. We build two sequences of polytropic stellar models and investigate how damping depends on rotation rate (from the non-rotating case to the mass-shedding limit) and compactness. Our study focuses on the quasi-radial $l=0$ $F$ mode and the $l=1,2,3$ fundamental modes, covering a dataset of 288 perturbed stellar models. For all modes and chosen viscosities, the BDNK runs show that oscillations decay within a few milliseconds, much faster than in the perfect fluid case. The $F$ mode damping is dominated by bulk viscosity, consistent with its global compression of the star, while the $l=2$ and $l=3$ modes are mainly damped by shear viscosity. The $l=1$ mode is largely insensitive to both viscosity coefficients, and its decay rate is dominated by numerical dissipation. Rotation renders the $F$ mode sensitive to shear viscosity. Since the inherent numerical damping does not affect the slopes of the decay rates, our viscous sensitivity estimates faithfully identify the dominant damping mechanism for each mode, shear or bulk viscosity, and reveal robust trends with rotation rate and compactness.
item.dc:creator: \'Oscar H. Petit, Jos\'e A. Font

item.title: Gravitational waves in hierarchical triples with lensing and relativistic orbits
item.description: arXiv:2611.29638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Binary black holes (BBH) may be formed near galactic nuclei. If such BBH systems exist, modulations to the gravitational waveform through time delays, lensing, and angular momentum precession could allow the presence of the third body to be measured in this system. In this letter, we advance the modeling for hierarchical triples by carefully including new relativistic lensing, aberration, and polarization terms. We show that the gravitational waves from this system can be computed exactly in the geometric optics limit by ray tracing the null geodesics and parallel transporting their polarization without a weak-field expansion. Our construction evolves the inner binary as if it were a post-Newtonian signal, and computes the environmental modulations efficiently with elliptic integrals. We find that this method improves the accuracy of such a triple waveform significantly compared to previous post-Newtonian approximations, and allows numerically efficient computation of the modulations. This lays the groundwork for future hierarchical triple waveform codebases, which can be used in LISA parameter estimation and detectability.
item.dc:creator: Brian C. Seymour, Fabiano Feleppa, Luka Vujeva, Johan Samsing

item.title: Ionization of gravitational atoms by a companion-sourced Yukawa potential
item.description: arXiv:2611.29939v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superradiant instabilities around rotating black holes can produce clouds of ultralight bosons bound by the black hole's gravitational field. A binary companion can ionize these clouds by driving transitions into continuum states in the black hole's 1/r gravitational potential, extracting energy and angular momentum from the orbit. We investigate how a companion-sourced Yukawa interaction modifies this process. At weak coupling, the interference term between the gravitational and Yukawa transition amplitudes provides the leading correction to the ionization power. For the orbital frequencies here, an attractive interaction enhances continuum ionization and accelerates the inspiral, whereas a repulsive interaction has the opposite effect. At larger coupling, the pure Yukawa contribution to the ionization power becomes increasingly important and can compete with the gravitational contribution, particularly for lighter mediators. Comparing continuum ionization with off-resonant bound-state mixing, we find that continuum ionization can halt superradiant growth at a substantially smaller Yukawa coupling. At their respective critical couplings, the Yukawa interaction provides the dominant contribution to cloud depletion in both channels. Finally, we calculate the phase correction to gravitational waves due to continuum ionization and characterize how the chirp-rate response varies with frequency near the thresholds at which successive orbital harmonics open continuum-ionization channels.
item.dc:creator: Yi Wang, Jiayi Yao

item.title: Void inside the horizon: connecting the third-quantized vacuum to a classical spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2611.29963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the emergence of a classical spacetime from a quantum-gravitational vacuum within the framework of third quantization applied to the black hole interior. Following the canonical quantization of the Kantowski--Sachs spacetime, one can construct a wave packet that explains the classical interior of a Schwarzschild black hole. This wave packet should be extended to the classical singularity. To avoid this, one can introduce an analytic continuation and the Euclidean wave function. This is not an analytic continuation of the spacetime, but of the superspace. To give this a suitable meaning, it is reasonable to introduce the concept of the third quantization. In this aspect, the Euclidean analytic continuation of the superspace explains the on-shell trajectory connecting the third-quantized vacuum state to a coherent classical geometry. Finally, we discuss how nonlinear self-interactions and baby-universe wormhole couplings must be incorporated into the third-quantized action to dynamically drive this transition.
item.dc:creator: Dong-han Yeom

item.title: The type-II double copy for relativistic Rindler fluids
item.description: arXiv:2611.30242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Within the Weyl double copy framework, we study a mixed single-copy construction for the Petrov type-II geometry of first-order relativistic Rindler fluids. Working on a common fixed flat Rindler background with consistent spinor conventions and a real field strength representation, we algebraically factorize the Weyl spinor into two symmetric rank-two Maxwell spinors and test the Maxwell equations and the zeroth copy scalar equation up to the first order in the relativistic gradient expansion. We separate the degeneration parameter from the gradient expansion parameter and analyze the continuous degeneration to the Petrov type-D and type-N branches as the complex shear and vorticity tend to zero, together with the preservation of the accuracy of the Maxwell and scalar field equations along each path. We also compare the relativistic construction with the nonrelativistic case.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Cheng Wang, Jing-Rui Zhang, Yun-Long Zhang

item.title: Segre Classification as a Framework for Generating Exact Solutions in Static Cylindrical Spacetimes with Levi-Civita Matching
item.description: arXiv:2611.30258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The main objective of this article is to analyze cylindrically symmetric static spacetime based on the Segre classification, where each Segre type corresponds to a set of canonical forms of Ricci spinors represented by Newman-Penrose scalars. The surviving Segre types of trace-free Ricci tensor in the cylindrical geometry are $[1,(111)]$, $[1,1(11)]$, $[(1,1)11]$, $[1,111]$, $[(1,11)1]$, $[(1,1)(11)]$ and $[(1,111)]$. Different combinations of eigenvalues and eigenvectors formed via Segre classification aid in understanding the distribution of matter and energy within that particular kind. Solutions are presented for the isotropic type $[1,(111)]$, for the anisotropic type $[1,1(11)]$, where a new metric function is introduced, and for type $[1,111]$, where all three pressures differ and the Krori-Barua functions are used. They satisfy the physical and stability criteria, namely the Zeldovich condition, causality condition, energy conditions and adiabatic index. The types $[(1,1)11]$ and $[(1,11)1]$ have $\rho=-P_r$ and give dark energy like configurations in which the strong energy condition is violated in the core, the latter having the tachyonic fluid form of the energy momentum tensor. For type $[(1,1)(11)]$, a charged solution in the presence of a non-null electromagnetic field is obtained and joined to an electrovac exterior. Matching with the Levi-Civita exterior shows that the vanishing of the radial pressure at the boundary is equivalent to the Darmois conditions. The C-energy and the curvature invariants are evaluated for each solution, and the results are compared with earlier works.
item.dc:creator: Wardah Aroosh Afzal, Tooba Feroze

item.title: Imprints of quantum space in the ringdown phase of Kerr black holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.30391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate quantum-space corrections to the gravitational quasinormal modes (QNMs) of Kerr black holes within the framework of noncommutative geometry. The analysis employs a pseudo-semi-Killing Drinfeld twist, which preserves the classical Kerr geometry as an exact background solution while introducing nontrivial quantum corrections to linearized gravitational perturbations. Working to first order in the black hole spin and the quantum deformation parameter, including their mixed contribution, we derive a Schr\"odinger-like master equation for axial gravitational perturbations with a frequency- and spin-dependent effective potential. We compute the fundamental QNM frequencies using the WKB approximation and Leaver's continued-fraction method.Our results reveal corrections to the QNM oscillation frequencies and damping rates arising from rotation, pure quantum effects, and their interplay.To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic analysis of gravitational metric perturbations in a noncommutative Kerr black hole spacetime using a Drinfeld twist, extending prior work beyond the Schwarzschild case. Our findings demonstrate that quantum deformation effects alter both the oscillation frequencies and damping rates of quasinormal modes, with spin-quantum coupling introducing additional spin-dependent corrections to the Kerr QNM spectrum. Using a Kerr-anchored phenomenological prescription, we estimate the fractional frequency and damping-time shifts for selected merger remnants from the GWTC-3 and GWTC-5.0 catalogs. These estimates illustrate the potential signatures of quantum corrections in gravitational-wave ringdown.
item.dc:creator: Nikola Herceg, Tajron Juri\'c, A. Naveena Kumara, Andjelo Samsarov, Ivica Smoli\'c, Kumar S. Gupta

item.title: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals: accessing generic orbits
item.description: arXiv:2611.30414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRI) are a significant gravitational wave source and a target for the upcoming LISA mission. Computations of the fluxes of conserved quantities, such as energy and angular momentum, are a critical part of modeling EMRI waveforms and can be performed using a frequency domain formalism to solve the Teukolsky equation. This requires computations of large numbers of mode amplitudes, many of which are negligible. However, it is unknown ex ante which can be safely skipped. We present a machine learning approach to estimate the dominant radial mode number as a function of the remaining mode numbers and apply it to reduce the number of unnecessary computations in EMRI flux calculation.
item.dc:creator: Ond\v{r}ej Zelenka, Michal Straten\'y, Petr Kotla\v{r}\'ik, Georgios Lukes-Gerakopoulos

item.title: Post-Newtonian expansion of the energy and angular momentum flux radiated to infinity: Eccentric-equatorial orbits about a Kerr black hole
item.description: arXiv:2611.30437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present analytical expressions for the energy and angular momentum fluxes radiated to infinity by a (nonspinning) point mass in an eccentric-equatorial orbit about a Kerr black hole. These results build upon our previous work involving point masses on eccentric orbits about a Schwarzschild black hole. We now adopt the Teukolsky formalism in first-order black hole perturbation theory to extend our methods to Kerr. We obtain the expressions using the method of Mano, Suzuki, and Takasugi, which provides infinite-series analytical solutions to the Teukolsky equation that we generate using Mathematica. The expressions presented are obtained as a double expansion in the post-Newtonian (PN) compactness parameter $1/p$, where $p$ is the dimensionless semi-latus rectum, and in the eccentricity $e$, up to 10PN and $e^{20}$, extending beyond prior 6PN and $e^{16}$ results available for generic orbits. We characterize how the PN flux coefficients depend on the black hole spin $a$ and $e$, and find a set of spin-dependent components that can be resummed as closed-form expressions in $e$. The analytical expressions are then validated with numerical comparisons against high-precision sample results from an independent Teukolsky code and with a broader set of numerically interpolated values derived from a flux data set produced with the same code. For $a=0.9M$, the numerically evaluated 10PN fluxes match current interpolated flux grids ($\sim10^{-7}$) for $p\gtrsim20$ to $75$ as $e$ ranges from $0.1$ to $0.7$, where they could replace Teukolsky-code results.
item.dc:creator: Jezreel C. Castillo, Christopher Munna, Zachary Nasipak, J. David Brown, Charles R. Evans

item.title: Dissipative Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars from Viscous Heating
item.description: arXiv:2611.30466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the leading low-frequency dissipative tidal response of nonrotating relativistic neutron stars. We formulate the response in a worldline effective field theory. We determine the linear dissipative Love number in two complementary ways: from the redshifted viscous entropy production inside the star and from the imaginary, frequency-odd part of the exterior metric. The first method reduces the calculation to an integral over the static equilibrium tide; the second provides an independent check. We apply our approach to publicly available equations of state and assess the corresponding correction to the gravitational-wave phase of neutron-star binaries. For an equal-mass $1.4+1.4M_\odot$ binary with both stars at a redshifted temperature $T_\infty=10^5\,\mathrm K$ and a standard electron shear viscosity, tidal dissipation shifts the gravitational-wave phase by less than $10^{-3}$ cycles between $20\,{\rm Hz}$ and $1\,{\rm kHz}$ for the four equations of state considered. Including the resulting rise in the stars' temperature in a simple thermal model reduces the shift below $10^{-6}$ cycles. For the viscosity model considered here, shear-viscous tidal dissipation in cold neutron stars is negligible for gravitational-wave phasing. This suggests that a measurable dissipative tidal signature would have to come from a different mechanism.
item.dc:creator: Nikola Savi\'c, Filippo Vernizzi

item.title: Geometric distinguishability of two-source gravitational-wave signals from the extrinsic geometry of the single-source waveform manifold
item.description: arXiv:2611.30560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Overlapping gravitational-wave signals can produce strong degeneracies in which a multi-source waveform is accurately represented by a single effective source. We formulate this source-confusion problem geometrically by treating the family of single-source waveforms as an embedded manifold in the noise-weighted detector Hilbert space. We introduce the distance-to-manifold statistic, defined as the minimum residual obtained by fitting a waveform with the single-source model, and show that its squared value is directly related to the maximized likelihood difference between two-source and single-source hypotheses in the noiseless limit. For two sources with nearby parameters, perturbative minimization demonstrates that the effective single-source fit absorbs all leading tangent-space deformations. The first irreducible residual lies in the normal space of the waveform manifold and is governed by its second fundamental form. We validate our approach using a six-parameter frequency-domain inspiral model with a LISA-like time-delay-interferometry response. Direct optimization reproduces the predicted quartic scaling over the numerically resolved regime, while two-dimensional confusion-zone maps reveal strongly anisotropic distinguishability boundaries. These results establish extrinsic waveform-manifold curvature as a coordinate-independent diagnostic of local multi-source confusion and provide a practical framework for identifying parameter-space directions in which overlapping gravitational-wave sources are most difficult to resolve.
item.dc:creator: Cezar Valentin Ionescu, Paul Adrian Gog\^{\i}\c{t}\u{a}, Laurentiu Ioan Caramete, Ana Caramete

item.title: The Science Chapter of the Einstein Telescope Geometry Comparison Report
item.description: arXiv:2611.30570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This is the Scientific Added Value Chapter of the Einstein Telescope (ET) Geometry Comparison Report, commissioned from the ET Organization by the ET Board of Governmental Representatives. We compare three configurations: a single-site 10-km triangle ($\Delta$) and two 15-km L-shaped detectors (2L) at widely separated sites, either nearly aligned or misaligned. We use metrics representative of the ET science case: compact-binary populations, dense matter, cosmography, stochastic backgrounds, multimessenger astronomy, fundamental physics, and continuous and burst sources. All three configurations deliver the ET science case, but they excel in different areas. For most sensitivity-driven science, the 2L configurations outperform the $\Delta$. The misaligned 2L is best for localizing and characterizing individual sources, multimessenger astronomy, and bright-siren cosmology. The nearly aligned 2L is best for stochastic backgrounds. The $\Delta$ localizes sources better than the aligned 2L and performs comparably to both 2L configurations for continuous and burst sources and at kilohertz frequencies. A 2L orientation of $30^\circ$ is a good compromise between stochastic-background sensitivity and localization. We validate Fisher information matrix (FIM) forecasts against Bayesian inference for $\sim550$ binary black hole and neutron star-black hole signals. Despite substantial differences, the FIM shows no systematic preference for either configuration for intrinsic parameters. For distance and sky localization, the FIM cannot capture multimodality and long-range correlations, leading to larger discrepancies, which however do not affect the ranking. Adding Cosmic Explorer to the network improves the reach of all three ET configurations, especially in volume localization and characterization of high-redshift sources. Differences between geometries shrink, but the ranking is largely unchanged.
item.dc:creator: Alessandra Buonanno, Federico De Lillo, Arnab Dhani, Tim Dietrich, Ulyana Dupletsa, Archisman Ghosh, Ish Gupta, Jan Harms, Francesco Iacovelli, Vuk Mandic, Harsh Narola, B. S. Sathyaprakash, Chris Van den Broeck, Haowen Zhong

item.title: Constraining Regular Black Hole Models with the Effective Field Theory treatment of General Relativity
item.description: arXiv:2611.30616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present a method for using perturbative predictions from treating general relativity as an effective field theory to constrain non-perturbative approaches to quantum gravity in black hole contexts. We start by reviewing a known result from this framework, which estimates the first quantum corrections to the interaction energy of a static particle near a black hole. We then propose a way to test non-perturbative quantum black hole models - specifically those formulated as modified Schwarzschild metrics, also known as regular black holes - against this perturbative result. To illustrate, we apply our method to the Hayward metric, showing that it does not align with the perturbative prediction, and we identify the most general metric that can reproduce the expected result.
item.dc:creator: Sami Viollet

item.title: Central charges as black-hole hair in weakly coupled trace-anomaly gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.30708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study black holes in Gabadadze's weakly coupled effective theory of the gravitational trace anomaly, keeping both the Euler and the Weyl central charges. We prove that a constant anomalyon on any Ricci-flat geometry, the Kerr family included, solves the full theory if and only if the two central charges coincide. Otherwise, the black holes continuously connected to this branch carry scalar hair whose charge is fixed by the surface gravity, the horizon topology and the difference of central charges alone: maximally supersymmetric matter leaves black holes bald, the Standard Model and photon-dominated sectors produce hair of definite sign, and conformal collider bounds confine it to a universal window. Electric charge separates the two anomaly invariants: the hair reverses sign at a critical charge-to-mass ratio set by the ratio of central charges, its extremal value retains only the Weyl charge, and the Euler charge governs the near-horizon growth of the anomalyon. For every unitary matter sector, the hair regular at the event horizon diverges at the Cauchy horizon. Finally, once the higher-derivative Weyl operator is order-reduced, the background, the anomalyon-graviton mixing and all propagation speeds depend only on the difference of central charges, which extends the no-ghost and Laplacian stability conditions to the full anomaly.
item.dc:creator: Francisco Tello-Ortiz, A. V\'asquez, Kazuharu Bamba, Ghulam Mustafa

item.title: Detecting Frame Dragging Effect with Next-Generation Spaceborne Clocks in a LEO-DRO Satellite Configuration
item.description: arXiv:2611.30726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Our approach employs a satellite constellation comprising one satellite in low Earth orbit (LEO) and one satellite in distant retrograde orbit (DRO). This configuration is designed to enhance the sensitivity to the Earth's rotation-induced frame-dragging signal while providing a stable and gravitationally isolated frequency reference. We derive a complete relativistic formulation for the frequency comparison between LEO and DRO, incorporating the post-Newtonian metric, higher-order Earth multipoles, lunar and solar tidal potentials, and the gravitomagnetic vector potential. The frame-dragging signal is of order $10^{-20}$, a level that is becoming increasingly accessible with next-generation optical clocks. Recent advances in zero-dead-time strontium optical lattice clocks have demonstrated a fractional frequency instability of $2.9\times10^{-19}$ at an averaging time of 20,000~s, with an estimated one-day stability of $2.5\times10^{-19}$. With continued advances in clock stability, achieving fractional-frequency sensitivity at the $10^{-20}$ level appears feasible in the near term, potentially enabling the direct measurement of a frame-dragging signal of the same order. Such a measurement would constrain Earth's gravitomagnetic field, enabling future investigations of gravitomagnetic effects on Einstein clock synchronization.
item.dc:creator: Li-Fang Li, Hanlin Song, Xing Bian, Tong Liu, Shao-Jiang Wang, Song He, Yang Li, Jiaxing Leng, Ziren Luo, Peng Xu, Rong-Gen Cai

item.title: Analytic $k$-essence Inflation
item.description: arXiv:2611.30846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we develop a fully analytic $k$-essence inflation solution which is compatible with the observational constraints on inflation, without the need for the slow-roll assumption being imposed dynamically in the field equations. The analytic solution is obtained for a kinetic scalar sector of the form $K(X)= \frac{X^n}{X_s^{n-1}}$ and for the scalar field satisfying a tracking condition $\dot{\phi}^2=\gamma H^{-m}$. For this class of theories, the sound speed of the primordial curvature perturbations is constant, so no gradient instabilities occur in the theory. The Hubble rate, the scale factor and the scalar field can be analytically expressed as functions of the cosmic time, and the observational indices of inflation depend solely on the parameters $n$ and $m$. The resulting evolution is inflationary and it develops a pressure singularity a few $e$-foldings after the end of inflation. However, using qualitative and quantitative numerical arguments, we show that the pressure singularity is classically avoided when the matter fluids of radiation and cold dark matter are taken into account.
item.dc:creator: V. K. Oikonomou

item.title: Schwarzschild-de Sitter space is not rigid
item.description: arXiv:2611.31019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Starting from any compact sub-extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region with positive cosmological constant, we construct a family of static axisymmetric vacuum solutions with two additional black-hole horizons, each of prescribed area. All horizons and the symmetry axis are regular, and the metric and lapse are real analytic up to the boundary. As the mass parameter tends to zero, the metric and lapse converge smoothly to the reference solution away from two antipodal points on its sphere of maximal lapse. Rescaling near either added horizon yields the Schwarzschild spatial metric in the limit. For small prescribed mass, the lapse attains its maximum precisely on one equatorial circle. Its Hessian is negative definite in the transverse plane, with the smaller eigenvalue magnitude asymptotic to a positive constant times the added mass. Nearby regular level sets are tori. The proof combines gluing at separated scales with uniform elliptic estimates. An integral condition removes infinitesimal translations of each Schwarzschild model, while a localized tensor source restores solvability of the linearized equation. Matching the local Schwarzschild corrections to a global Green tensor identifies the leading source coefficients. Reflection makes these coefficients equal, and varying the common radial position of the centers makes them vanish. A radial Green function and the heat equation on the sphere determine the angular variation of the lapse and the geometry of its maximum set.
item.dc:creator: Philippe G. LeFloch, Luc Rozoy

item.title: Lyapunov Stability of a Schwarzschild Black Hole Surrounded by the Kiselev Anisotropic Fluid
item.description: arXiv:2611.31035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the geodesic structure and the stability of circular orbits around a Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a Kiselev anisotropic fluid, characterised by the equation-of-state parameter $\omega$ and the normalisation parameter $N$. We consider six representative values, $\omega=-1,-2/3,-1/3,0,1/3$ and $1$, over the admissible range of $N$ determined by the horizon structure, including the corresponding extremal limits. Using the effective potentials for null and timelike geodesics, we determine the photon sphere, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) and the outermost stable circular orbit (OSCO), and examine their stability through coordinate-time Lyapunov exponents. The photon sphere is unstable for all values of $\omega$ and $N$ considered. Its instability weakens with increasing $N$ for $\omega\leq0$ and vanishes at extremality for $\omega=-1$ and $-2/3$, whereas it varies non-monotonically with $N$ for $\omega=1/3$ and strengthens for $\omega=1$. For $\omega=-1$ and $-2/3$, stable circular orbits are confined between the ISCO and the OSCO, which merge at a critical value of $N$ beyond which no stable circular orbits exist. In contrast, for $\omega\geq-1/3$ stable circular orbits exist at all radii beyond the ISCO, whose location varies with $N$. We also derive a closed-form expression for the squared coordinate-time Lyapunov exponent $(\lambda_t^T)^2$, valid for arbitrary $\omega$, whose sign changes exactly at the ISCO and OSCO, so that the Lyapunov criterion reproduces the boundaries of stable circular motion. The Schwarzschild--de Sitter, mass-shifted Schwarzschild and Reissner--Nordstr\"om geometries are recovered as special cases, and the results may have implications for black-hole shadows, thin accretion discs and quasi-periodic oscillations.
item.dc:creator: Saswati Roy, Paramita Debnath, Shubham Kala, Hemwati Nandan

item.title: Relativistic dynamical friction and accretion for Kerr black holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.31061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) observed by LISA will probe the environments of massive black holes (BHs), including the dark matter (DM) overdensities expected to form around them. We compute the relativistic dynamical friction and accretion experienced by a non-spinning compact object on circular equatorial orbits around a Kerr BH embedded in a collisionless DM distribution, extending previous results in Schwarzschild. The DM is modeled as a spike grown adiabatically from an initial Hernquist profile, and the momentum transfer is obtained by integrating relativistic scattering and capture cross sections over the full, generically anisotropic phase space seen by the secondary. Far from the primary the friction tracks the local DM density, which increases with spin. Near the innermost stable circular orbit of rapidly spinning BHs $(a\gtrsim 0.37)$, however, frame dragging forces bound DM particles to co-rotate, so that the secondary is overtaken by the surrounding medium: the friction weakens and eventually reverses sign where the DM density peaks. We show that a similar reversal can be mimicked around a non-rotating BH if the initial halo carries large net angular momentum, although this requires anisotropies beyond those found in cosmological simulations. We also show that commonly used Chandrasekhar-like prescriptions, which depend only on the local density, can overestimate the friction force. Our results demonstrate that the full phase-space structure of the environment must be included when modeling DM effects on EMRIs.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Speeney, Soumodeep Mitra, Emanuele Berti, Andrea Maselli, Sumanta Chakraborty

item.title: Enhancing eccentricity through tidal resonance in binary neutron star systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.31172v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Orbital eccentricity of binary neutron star systems is a key parameter to reveal their formation history. Since binaries formed in isolation are expected to circularize long before merger, measurable eccentricity suggests dynamical formation in dense stellar environments. However, using numerical-relativity simulations, we show that eccentricity can be introduced in the late inspiral of an initially quasicircular binary, due to the $f$-mode resonance of one of the stars. We simulate the merger of two highly spinning neutron stars, one star spinning prograde and the other retrograde. Persistent tidal resonance with the $f$ mode of the retrograde-spinning star is observed, accompanied by a gradual change of its spin due to angular momentum transfer from the orbit. This spin change can be well explained by a simple resonance locking model that accounts for the spin-dependent shift of the $f$-mode frequency. These findings reveal an origin of eccentricity in binary neutron stars that is independent of their formation history and provide important information for modeling binary neutron star dynamics with rapidly spinning stars.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Markin, Natalie Williams, Tim Dietrich

item.title: Optimal Statistic for a Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background using Pulsar-Timing--Astrometry Cross Correlations
item.description: arXiv:2611.31196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Astrometric measurements have emerged as a viable probe of gravitational waves (GWs), complementing pulsar timing searches by providing overlapping and higher GW frequency coverage. At its core, the search for GWs using astrometry is very similar to the search with pulsar timing data: GWs induce a change in pulse arrival times along the line of sight to a pulsar and a transverse angular deflection in the apparent position of a star. In analogy to pulsar timing, we develop a correlation statistic between pairs of stellar deflections for astrometry to search for a stochastic GW background. With a common formalism for both astrometry and pulsar timing, we also develop the cross-correlation statistic between stellar deflections and pulsar timing residuals. We estimate the signal-to-noise ratios from the correlation statistics and provide scaling laws in the weak- and intermediate-signal regimes.
item.dc:creator: Kimberly K. Boddy, Jeffrey S. Hazboun, Kris Pardo

item.title: On the existence of constants of motion for multipolar test-body dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.31200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the conservative equations of motion of an extended test body, with force and torque sourced by spin-induced and adiabatic tidal multipoles of arbitrary order, are the flow of the Hamiltonian $H=-\tfrac12\mu^2+\mu U$, where $\mu$ is the body's kinematic mass and all multipoles enter through a covariant scalar potential $U$. For such bodies, a certain notion of mass and a spin norm are shown to be exactly conserved, at all multipolar orders and in any background. We then apply our framework to the Kerr spacetime, and construct extensions of the Carter and R\"udiger constants through hexadecapolar order (quartic in spin). They are found to exist if, and only if, the body's multipoles are those of a Kerr black hole. Together with the energy and angular momentum, they make the dynamics of a spinning test black hole in Kerr perturbatively integrable through that order. Lastly, at the next, quintic-in-spin order, an analytic criterion implemented numerically reveals that neither constant admits a continuation, for any conservative multipoles. In the conservative, test-body limit, black-hole binaries thus carry a dynamical hidden symmetry shared by no other compact objects, which persists to high multipolar order but ultimately breaks.
item.dc:creator: Paul Ramond

item.title: Horizon mergers and initial test-charge acceleration in charged black-hole geometries with anisotropic sources
item.description: arXiv:2611.28095v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study horizon mergers and the initial radial acceleration of charged test particles in static, spherically symmetric black-hole geometries with a string cloud, a Kiselev power-law component, or a logarithmic profile conventionally. After separating the Maxwell contribution, the effective environmental stress tensors are anisotropic and are not identified with homogeneous quintessence or pressureless cold dark matter. Using a common mass-function formulation, we derive the horizon-merger conditions and classify the Kiselev branches. In this family, the inner-event merger charge provides only an upper bound: three distinct positive horizons can additionally require a positive lower charge bound associated with the event-cosmological merger. For a test particle released from rest relative to a static observer, we derive the local charge-to-mass threshold for outward initial acceleration. Writing $\lambda=q/\mu$ and $z=Q/Q_{\rm ext}$, where $Q_{\rm ext}$ is the inner-event merger charge, the subextremal string-cloud threshold has infimum $1/z$, approached only at infinity. For the subextremal logarithmic profile, the threshold exceeds unity throughout the finite exterior and attains a finite global minimum. For $\alpha/M=0.4$ and $Q/M=1.2$, this minimum is $\lambda_*\simeq1.251125$. In a nondegenerate Kiselev static patch, the neutral balance radius is unique and radially unstable. Density matching supplies conditional profile normalizations, not observational fits. For the logarithmic profile, the integration parameter is distinguished from the mass combination inferred from circular motion. These results characterize geometric horizon bounds and test-particle dynamics; they do not establish a two-black-hole force law or a mechanism for cosmic acceleration, nor do they constitute a test of the Weak Gravity Conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Noori Gashti, Mohammad Ali S. Afshar, Mohammad Reza Alipour

item.title: Dual Horizon-MAD: A New Mode of Binary Black Hole Magnetically Arrested Accretion with Saturated Horizon Magnetic Fluxes and Intermittent Minidisks
item.description: arXiv:2611.28237v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reliable first-principles predictions of multimessenger signals from inspiralling supermassive binary black holes (SMBBHs) require magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations in full general relativity (GR) that resolve the accretion flow down to the black hole horizons. However, performing such simulations long enough to relax the magnetohydrodynamics near the BBHs is computationally challenging and a source of uncertainty in modeling efforts. In this work, we present the longest MHD simulation of circumbinary disk (CBD) accretion onto a SMBBH in full GR. The equal-mass, quasicircular, nonspining BBH starts at an initial separation of $d/M=30$ and evolves over $\sim56$ orbits ($t \simeq 52,000 \, GM/c^3$), relaxing the magnetic field dynamics within the CBD cavity. After $\sim 23$ orbits and persistent magnetically arrested minidisks, the accretion enters a new magnetically arrested mode which we call dual horizon-MAD (DH-MAD). In DH-MAD, the dimensionless horizon magnetic fluxes remain saturated at $\phi_{BH}\sim 20$ driving magnetic flux eruptions from the vicinity of the BH horizons, and the vertical magnetic flux in the cavity saturates, but no flux eruptions occur at the cavity-CBD boundary. During this DH-MAD phase, there is also a shift in the total mass accretion rate variability, which exhibits a periodicity of $f\sim 1.8 f_{\rm orb}$, while the accretion rate modulation on the individual black holes occurs almost at the orbital period, $f\sim 0.9 f_{\rm orb}$. $\phi_{BH}$ also exhibits a robust periodicity at $f\sim 0.4 f_{\rm orb}$, suggesting that quasiperiodic nonthermal emission from magnetic reconnection near the horizons could be a smoking gun electromagnetic counterpart to inspiraling SMBBHs. Finally, minidisks around the BHs become intermittent in the DH-MAD phase, even at a separation of $d/M = 24$, likely due to the large plasma magnetization in the optically thin cavity.
item.dc:creator: Vikram Manikantan, Vasileios Paschalidis

item.title: Relativistic Hydrodynamics as an Intersection Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.28735v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ideal relativistic hydrodynamics admits a covariant description as an intersection problem in a symplectic space associated with spacetime. The independent fields are differential forms of degrees 0,1,3,4. Spacetime diffeomorphisms and shifts of the momentum one-form act Hamiltonianly; the zero locus of their moment map is a coisotropic subvariety encoding the transport equations. The spacetime metric and equation of state determine a Lagrangian submanifold, whose intersection with the coisotropic subvariety is precisely the Lichnerowicz--Carter system. We explain the geometric meaning of the canonical flow parameter, derive circulation and Ertel invariants directly from the constraints, and identify energy--momentum conservation with covariance of the constitutive Lagrangian. The nonrelativistic limit and a relation of entropy-level helicity to split Calabi--Yau geometry are briefly indicated.
item.dc:creator: Nikita Nekrasov, Paul Wiegmann

item.title: Scale-dependent Dark Matter in a Multi-component Cosmological Framework: Distinct Components Governing Galactic and Cosmological Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.29007v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work we generalize the concept of scale-dependent equation of state dark matter from galactic to cosmological scales. At galactic scales, the scale-dependent equation of state which successfully describes dark matter dominated galaxies has a nearly isothermal equation of state of the form $P(r)=K(r)\rho(r)$, where the entropy function $K(r)$ is radius dependent and slowly varying with the galactic radius. Using appropriate theoretical arguments, the successful galactic scale dark matter model is generalized to have a universal equation of state of the form $\langle P(\chi)\rangle =\langle \rho(\chi)\rangle \langle \sigma_{DM}^2\rangle$, where $\chi$ is the scale of the system under study and it can describe cosmological or galactic scales and $\sigma_{DM}$ is the characteristic velocity dispersion of dark matter at the relevant scales. This results to the entropy function behaving universally as $K(\chi)=\langle \sigma_{DM}^2\rangle$. We investigate the cosmological implications of scale-dependent equation of state dark matter, and we conclude that this scale-dependent equation of state dark matter cannot be the sole component of dark matter in the Universe. Also the second aim of this work is to provide a sufficient explanation for the question why $K_0$ changes for each galaxy, where $K_0$ is the value of $K(r)$ at intermediate and large radii from the core of the galaxy. Furthermore, we introduce the concept of having distinct dark matter components which cluster differently, and thus controlling differently the dynamics of the Universe at various scales. Scale-dependent equation of state dark matter can control the galactic scales, while another component can dominate at cosmological scales and thus control the Universe at cosmological scales.
item.dc:creator: V. K. Oikonomou

item.title: Sound of Keplerian binaries in a homogeneous Newtonian fluid background
item.description: arXiv:2611.29183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate the dissipation due to sound-wave emission from a Keplerian binary embedded in a homogeneous Newtonian fluid background at rest in the binary center-of-mass frame within linear perturbation theory. Rather than starting from the local wake force, we treat the binary as a localized periodic mass source and compute the sound-wave fluxes carried away by the medium. The time-averaged energy, linear-momentum, and angular-momentum fluxes are obtained from Noether currents of the fluid perturbations. For a classical inviscid barotropic Newtonian fluid, retaining the self-gravity of density perturbations while adopting the Jeans prescription, we derive explicit flux formulas for circular and eccentric binaries with arbitrary mass ratio. This formulation also clarifies the ultraviolet behavior of point sources: in a nondispersive fluid, the harmonic sum becomes cutoff-sensitive precisely when at least one component becomes supersonic. We examine explicitly how finite source size removes this divergence using a uniform-sphere model and relate the resulting regularization to a corresponding effective harmonic cutoff. The associated secular eccentricity evolution exhibits circularization in the subsonic regime when the fluid self-gravity is sufficiently weak but can change sign outside this regime, with eccentricity growth in the strictly supersonic UV limit. For a Schr\"odinger-Poisson quantum fluid, quantum pressure instead softens the high-frequency contribution and renders the point-source fluxes UV finite within the nonrelativistic regime; our numerical results further indicate eccentricity growth due to sound radiation over the parameter space explored. Finally, we translate orbital-decay measurements of two binary pulsars into order-of-magnitude bounds on the homogeneous quantum-fluid density surrounding each system.
item.dc:creator: Yan Cao, Mu-Chun Chen

item.title: Constraining Dehnen-inspired dark matter halo with S2 star's orbit
item.description: arXiv:2611.29245v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use the orbit of S2 star around Sagittarius A* to constrain three black hole backgrounds motivated by Dehnen profiles with inner slopes $\gamma=0$, $1$, and $5/2$, which are characterized by the scale radius $r_s$ and density $\rho_s$ of the dark matter halo. An exact turning-point integral gives the pericenter advance at finite eccentricity, and an exterior expansion identifies the leading halo contributions. A fifteen-parameter Bayesian analysis combines astrometric and spectroscopic observations with the measured precession parameter, from which we obtain the marginalized $1\sigma$ upper limits $r_s/M<0.236$, $0.168$, and $0.030$, and $\rho_sM^2<0.536$, $0.578$, and $0.004$, respectively. The leading halo monopole in the first two metrics is degenerate with the central mass. At fixed dynamical mass, their leading radial profile correction produces retrograde precession. The $\gamma=5/2$ metric introduces an additional angular deficit contribution, which enhances the precession response and accounts for its smaller parameter limits.
item.dc:creator: Qi Qi, Qiang Wu, Xiao-Mei Kuang

item.title: The Generalized Second Law from Fluctuation Theorems in a Quantum Reference Frame
item.description: arXiv:2611.29415v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the generalized second law (GSL) for black-hole exteriors undergoing unitary driving and relaxation on a fixed semifinite algebra. Wall's influential proof assumes semiclassical geometry and restricts fixed parent states to algebras of successive horizon cuts. We instead evolve the state on a fixed dressed exterior algebra. With complete characteristic data, the same semiclassical exterior supports both descriptions, analogous to the Heisenberg and Schr\"odinger pictures through state--operator duality. Using a gravitational charge as a quantum clock, we construct a modular crossed product with density operators whose trace entropy reproduces generalized entropy up to clock contributions. Our approach parallels thermodynamics in regulated field theory and formulates the GSL through a quantum channel fluctuation theorem (FT) for the open exterior. We develop three complementary formulations under specified dynamical assumptions. Separated unitary driving and relaxation combine modular work, the physical-process first law relating horizon absorption to area gain, and relative-entropy contraction through data processing. A time-local description accommodates simultaneous unitary driving and dissipation. A two-time surprisal FT treats the complete channel, identifies the nonunital correction, and yields a GSL bound for unital dressed evolution without resolving intermediate dynamics. Relaxation that does not mix distinct dressed-charge sectors and preserves the full dressed reference state is unital. Unitality is sufficient for this FT proof but is not necessary for the GSL along a particular evolution. The entropy bounds establish the GSL in a controlled slow-clock limit and quantify finite-width clock corrections.
item.dc:creator: Feng-Li Lin, Sayid Mondal

item.title: $p$-Harmonic gauge and the regularity of spacetime isometries
item.description: arXiv:2611.29643v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show every Lorentzian metric of class $C^{k,\alpha}$, where $k\in\mathbf{N}_0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$, admits local coordinates of class $C^{k+1,\alpha}$ all of whose coordinate functions are temporal functions that are harmonic with respect to a nonlinear $p$-wave operator, where $p\in(-\infty,1)$. Unlike the classical wave operator, this operator is elliptic on temporal functions. As an application, we show that an isometry between Lorentzian metrics of class $C^{k,\alpha}$ is of class $C^{k+1,\alpha}$.
item.dc:creator: Mathias Braun

item.title: Quadratic-in-spin scattering of compact bodies at fourth post-Minkowskian order
item.description: arXiv:2611.29670v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the fourth-post-Minkowskian scattering angle of aligned spinning compact bodies through quadratic spin at arbitrary velocity and mass ratio. We include spin-induced quadrupoles and radiation reaction, supplemented by curvature-squared spin-tidal terms. Three-loop worldline integrals yield closed forms in polylogarithms and elliptic integrals. Infrared poles cancel exactly, fixing the tail logarithm. We obtain a new post-Newtonian coefficient and third-order angular-momentum loss for general quadrupoles. The new input shifts resummed predictions for black-hole scattering.
item.dc:creator: Taushif Ahmed, Syed Mehedi Hasan

item.title: Boundary spectroscopy of hidden near-horizon reflection
item.description: arXiv:2611.30092v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A classical black hole horizon absorbs completely, and any deviation would be hidden in the bulk. For a scalar field in a rotating Ba\~nados-Teitelboim-Zanelli exterior, we derive an exact boundary response of a corotating passive wall near the horizon. An Airy filter gives its spectrum, and positive energy excludes growing modes. On any frequency band the response identifies a constant wall impedance and the wall position, which enter orthogonally with weights determined by the spectral function. The boundary thus sees a reflecting wall, whereas a perfect absorber is exponentially hidden.
item.dc:creator: Yiling Chen, Jiayue Yang, Zhen Zhong, Robert B. Mann, Jie Jiang, Ming Zhang

item.title: Superheavy gravitational dark matter from runaway bubble collisions
